principles: Composition over decoration: the slide is built from a small set of named components (accent-capped card, header-bar card, left-rule row, icon tile, phrase bar, centred statement) — an Amaris slide is one of those or a deliberate variation on one, never an improvisation.

No photography. The styling source of truth contains none in any slide that works, and the client removed it deliberately (2026-09-22). Where a visual is needed the order is: diagram, chart, icon tile, tinted panel, or generous whitespace with the circle field alone.

The circle field is the signature: 2-3 soft accent circles per slide, one large and bleeding off a corner, at 15-25 % opacity, always behind content, one accent each and never the same accent twice on a slide.
The hairline carries the structure: a 0.25 pt indigo keyline defines every card and panel. Elevation is a keyline, not a shadow.
Systematic clarity: Century Gothic alone, Regular 400 and Bold 700 only. No second family anywhere — no monospace, no serif, no intermediate weight.
Navy is the canvas only where it means something: cover, section divider, closing. #002060 is that canvas; #272774 is ink and keyline. They are not interchangeable.
Accents rotate positionally by default (01 blue, 02 purple, 03 mint, 04 yellow) and carry sector meaning ONLY when the content is actually about those sectors. Never both modes on one slide.
Generous margins: 0.58 in (42 pt) symmetric side margins, content never crowds the frame, and an empty well-set slide is on-brand.
signatureElements: Ambient circle layer — ONE geometry, TWO treatments, and the ring is the more common (44 rings vs 25 washes measured). Rings: hairline, unfilled, 2.2-12.1 in, indigo @25% or white @25-50%. Washes: soft fill, 2.0-7.0 in, 10-35% opacity, one accent each. Plus a saturated 0.8-1.1 in dot at 100%. 1-5 per surface, any corner, always bleeding, always behind content. Present on 31 of 34 layouts.

Keylines in three registers, all first-class — 0.25 pt #272774 hairline (31), 1.0 pt container (21), and #272774 at 25% (20), the quiet one that does most of the structural work. 0.5 pt white @20-50% on dark.
Accent-capped card — a 4-6 pt solid accent bar across the card's top edge, white or #FDF9F7 body, 8.6 pt radius, accent rotating blue/purple/mint/yellow.

Header-bar card — a solid accent block as the card header carrying bold text, with a keylined body beneath it. Text polarity inside is a choice, not a luminance rule: the source sets white on mint in one composite and navy ink on mint in another.
Left-rule row — full-width row with a 5-6 pt accent bar on its left edge, a 29-36 pt accent numeral and a bold indigo label. Its twin WITHOUT keyline or rule (soft shadow only) is equally attested.
Numbered step badge — a square (6 pt radius) carrying a bold numeral, filled either solid accent or tint-60.
Medallion — a functional circle, 0.37-1.97 in, accent-tint or #F6EEF7 lilac with a hairline ring, holding one icon. 89 of the deck's 164 circles are functional like this.
Nested tonal composition — a tint-80 panel containing tint-60 chips beside a white card: one hue at three depths. The monochrome-tonal accent mode.
Comparison pair — two mirrored cards with a circular connector straddling the gutter, label/value rows inside each, and a per-card tinted footer strip.
Asymmetric split — roughly 60/40, a row stack left and a visual slot right, with a large mixed-weight uppercase phrase beneath.
Inverted block — a solid #272674 card on the light canvas, often beside its identical blush twin. Rare and deliberate: 3 instances in the source.
Axis / timeline — medallions alternating above and below a 2 pt dashed indigo spine, each with an accent numeral and step label.
Phrase bar — a full-width 8.6 pt-radius bar, tint- or solid-navy-filled, text centred bold italic at 12-16 pt. At most one per surface.
Pill label — a fully-rounded solid-yellow chip carrying 10.5 pt bold indigo uppercase text; the cover's eyebrow.
Ghost numeral — 106 pt bold white at low opacity behind a section-divider title.
Ghost wordmark — the oversized outline AMARIS lockup cropped and bleeding off an edge at very low opacity; part of the ambient layer, not the footer.
Tracked uppercase eyebrow — 10-12 pt bold, typed uppercase (never an auto-caps attribute), letter-spaced 0.67 / 1.33 / 2.0 pt, plus a wide 6.0 pt register for small standalone labels.
Dark canvas #002060 flat for cover, section divider and closing; light canvas a vertical #FFFFFF → #FBF5F2 gradient everywhere else, never flat white.
antiPatterns: Photography of any kind — stock, sourced or generated. Removed from this brand's render path on 2026-09-22, and no image from the source deck is reused. A surface needing a visual gets a diagram, a chart, a medallion row, a tinted panel, or whitespace.
A flat white slide background — the light canvas is always the #FFFFFF → #FBF5F2 vertical gradient.
Using #272774 (or #272674) as a full-slide canvas — that is the ink and keyline colour; the dark canvas is #002060.
Filling an entire canvas with an accent — measured across 21 full-bleed canvases (17 light gradient, 4 navy), zero are accent. Accents cap, bar, badge, tint and fill CARDS; they are never the field.
A second type family — monospace footers, serif pull-quotes, or an intermediate Century Gothic weight (500/600 silently revert to Regular in Office).
Drop shadows used to express elevation — the keyline does that. A soft tight shadow on a stacked card is the only permitted shadow.
Mixing the two accent modes on one surface: positional rotation (01/02/03/04) and the sector mapping are alternatives, never simultaneous.
More than one phrase bar on a surface, or a phrase bar where there is no real takeaway.
An AMBIENT circle used as a container or carrying text — the ambient layer sits strictly behind content. (Functional medallions and badges ARE containers; they are a different primitive.)
The retired corporate-blank inferences: a 6 px blush rule on the cover's top edge, a monospace footer bar, or a navy scrim over a hero photograph. None appear anywhere in the 34 layouts or 23 slides.

evidence.note: No motion was captured from the static source PPTX. documentary-muted.label: Documentary Muted
documentary-muted.usage: Lightly desaturated editorial colour — the timeless default for content, section, and dense slides. Keeps corporate colour alive without going candid.

navy-duotone.label: Navy Duotone
navy-duotone.usage: Signature structural duotone for covers + hero moments — deep midnight shadows through indigo mids to blush highlights. The Amaris engineered-yet-warm signature; pairs with the navy scrim.

midnight-graded.label: Midnight Graded
midnight-graded.usage: Cool cinematic grade for technology/engineering imagery — indigo shadows, cool-blue highlights echoing the midnight gradient. Restrained, systematic.

blush-warm.label: Blush Warm
blush-warm.usage: Warm grade for people / life-sciences / softer section imagery — warm shadows to blush highlights. The human counterweight to the navy register; use sparingly.

expression.signatureMotion: The hairline orbit arc draws itself once across the frame in a single unhurried stroke, while the stepping-stone dot and headline settle in behind it in a quiet staggered fade.

compositionAxes.note: Primitives x axes x budget, NOT a template catalogue. Every combination these permit is evidenced in the source; layout (what sits where, in what proportion) is deliberately left to the authoring model. Reference, never bind — see presentation-grammar.md §0.
